items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: I thought of Pharoah Sanders because a lot of his music stayed on one chord for a long time.

ctx.x: [Scats]. And he refused to do that. But when I finally broke him down to where he would do it, he did the hell out of it. So some things happened automatically, some things happened just because they were written down and they played it exactly like it was written you know.

I was thinking, while you were just saying that, I thought of Pharoah Sanders because a lot of his music stayed on one chord for a long time. And I don’t have a question here except that it seems like you have to have a long attention span and just get into that rhythm so much that it doesn’t become boring. Because if it becomes boring it’s not going to work.
Right. Well I can’t think of this bass player’s name.
